page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place this instance consistently in the average performance tier across most compute and memory workloads. The Intel Xeon processor delivers a single-core stress-ng score of 1866.99 and a multi-core score of 30903.16, supported by 33 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction set extensions. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only large block bandwidth of 152.43 GB/sec and a write bandwidth of 69.06 GB/sec. In database simulation tests, the instance achieves 31.0 million operations per second for Redis SET operations and a PassMark database score of 14983.05. Notably, it demonstrates strong performance in small-model LLM text generation, achieving 297.4 tokens per second with a 135M parameter model.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced resource distribution, the ecs.u1-c1m4.8xlarge offers a stable and predictable environment for general-purpose workloads. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a cost-efficient choice for applications that do not require high-speed local scratch space or hardware acceleration. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, software compilation, static web serving, and medium-scale database operations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m4.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 128.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 instance provides a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio with no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. It features a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across standard compute and memory operations, with a PassMark CPU score of 34102.79 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 12613.0. The instance demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small language models, reaching 297.4 tokens per second. It is suited for general-purpose enterprise workloads, multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and database operations that require predictable CPU performance without the need for high-speed local NVMe storage.
